guard: the console's operator verbs reach the manager that hosts the seat, name the seat the operator asked for, kill the way the key says, and purge for real
why: The suite drives bin/cotal.ts, which imports @cotal-ai/cli from dist: a mutation must be built to be seen, and the tree must be rebuilt after the restore or dist keeps the mutant.
Each mutation is compile-clean and unique in the named file.

mutations.name: C1 :ps from one manager's answer instead of the scatter merge
mutations.find: return { ok: true, rows: s.instances.flatMap((i) => (i.reachable && !i.error ? ((i.data as ManagedRow[]) ?? []) : [])) };
mutations.replace: return { ok: true, rows: ((s.instances.find((i) => i.reachable && !i.error)?.data as ManagedRow[] | undefined) ?? []) };
mutations.expectRed: :ps lists the seats of both managers
mutations.cell: :ps lists the seats of both managers
mutations.note: The rows of the first manager that answered, which is what a single class-queue call would have returned.

mutations.name: C2 :status unpinned, answered by whichever manager is quickest
mutations.expectRed: :status on a seat no manager hosts is refused by the locate step, naming both reachable managers
mutations.cell: :status on a seat no manager hosts is refused by the locate step, naming both reachable managers
mutations.note: Deterministic: an unpinned inspect skips the locate, so a seat nobody hosts gets one manager's own not-found error instead of the locate's sentence counting both reachable managers. The 6/6 cell is behavioural evidence, not the kill.

mutations.name: C3 :spawn drops the requested name
mutations.find: const r = await ctx.control("start", identity ? { name: persona, identity } : { name: persona });
mutations.replace: const r = await ctx.control("start", { name: persona });
mutations.expectRed: :spawn shows the accepted name, the one requested rather than the persona's
mutations.cell: :spawn shows the accepted name, the one requested rather than the persona's

mutations.name: C4 f confirms a graceful stop
mutations.find: if (input === "f" || input === "F") return onConfirm({ force: true });
mutations.expectRed: f: the notice reports the force-kill
mutations.cell: f: the notice reports the force-kill

mutations.name: C5 purge confirmed but never sent
mutations.replace: void Promise.resolve({ ok: true, error: undefined as string | undefined }).then((r) => setNotice(r.ok ? "purged space history" : `purge: ${r.error ?? "failed"}`));
mutations.expectRed: purge: the space history is gone
mutations.cell: purge: the space history is gone
